newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin vows to fight wage delays, abuse of power.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin vows to fight wage delays, abuse of power.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, back in his Kremlin office after a heart operation in November, promised Russians on Wednesday that he will fight two major evils -- chronic delays in payment of wages and abuses by civil servants.

Yeltsin, 65, who returned to work on Monday after almost seven weeks of absence following quintuple bypass surgery, said in a radio address that wage delays were the most painful problem for his administration.
"The state's debt to the people is too high and the living standards are intolerably low," Yeltsin, whose voice sounded smooth and confident, said in his characteristic tough tone.
"I see my main duty in changing the situation," Yeltsin added. "I will use all powers which you gave to me by electing me the Russian president for this."
Wage delays which amount to trillions of roubles (billions of dollars) have triggered labour protests, including a nationwide strike of coal miners.
Top military officials have warned that morale in the armed forces has sunk to a dangerously low point as most officers have not been paid since the summer.
Yeltsin said stern measures to stop massive tax evasion and impose strong state control over the sale of alchohol could provide funds to help solve the problem of wage delays.
He said widespread misuse of state funds by civil servants also badly affected the state budget and added to the wage delay crisis.
"It's time to take measures against those who like living luxuriously at the state expense, or to be more exact at the expense of ordinary people," Yeltsin said.
He said he expected from the Prosecutor General and the Control Department of the presidential administration a detailed account of the steps they had taken to stop misuse of funds.
"Officials in charge will have to answer for wrongdoings," Yeltsin said. "If one is stealing he should go to jail, If one is incompetent he should resign.
Yeltsin, who won his second term in July polls, said in his five-minute address that throughout his illness he stayed in touch with the nation's problems.
"Those who think that while away from my office I lost touch with the country, its pain and its needs, are wrong, Yeltsin said.
"I know how difficult it is for people today, how difficult it is for the majority of families, and I will do everything I can to improve the situation in Russia."
Yeltsin said that the first shot in his new crusade will be made on Thursday at a meeting of a state commission set up to handle tax and non-payment crises.
"It's time to restore order on the alcohol market," he said. "Some make huge fortunes selling these goods without paying taxes."
"I am drafting special measures to correct this intolerable situation," Yeltsin added. "Tomorrow at the meeting of All-Russian Extraordinary Commission serious and strong steps will be taken."
Yeltsin said that restoring order was crucial for maintaining stability and called for a concerted effort by the president, government, parliament and local authorities.
